meta.message: Stopped at G1: 3 blocking question(s). See CLARIFICATION_REQUEST.md.
limitations: Offline mode: agents use deterministic strategies and domain blueprints (URL shortener, the bundled brownfield sample). Other domains/repositories need `--llm anthropic`.
Generated service uses SQLite and an in-process cache/queue: correct and tested, but not the production stack for the stated scale target (see scaling path).
No authentication/authorization on the API (documented risk).
Load/performance targets are design targets; no load test is executed by the pipeline.
Validation proves the generated tests pass and the contract matches; it cannot prove the tests are exhaustive - human review at G3 remains essential.

spec.raw: We need a links thing that's fast and has some stats. Maybe users too?
spec.title: URL shortener service
spec.intent: Let clients turn long URLs into short codes that redirect, persist them durably, and report how links are used.
functional: Create a short link for a valid http(s) URL via REST API
Redirect GET /{code} to the target URL
Fetch and delete link metadata via REST API
Record clicks and expose per-link analytics
Persist links and analytics durably across restarts
non_functional: Redirect hot path does no synchronous writes (analytics are asynchronous)
Short codes are non-sequential and not enumerable
Horizontally scalable stateless API tier; storage behind a repository interface
Consistent JSON error model; no internal details leaked on errors
Input validation on every external field (URL scheme, length, body size)
out_of_scope: User accounts / authentication (documented as a follow-up)
Link previews / malware scanning (documented as a risk)

ambiguities.question: Is the system a URL shortener (create short codes that redirect to long URLs)?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Determines the whole architecture; 'links thing' could also mean a bookmark manager.
options: yes, a URL shortener with redirects
ambiguities.default: yes, a URL shortener with redirects

ambiguities.question: What load should the design target?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Drives caching, storage choice, code-space size and the analytics pipeline.
options: 1k creates/s, 50k redirects/s at peak (design target); 100M links/year
ambiguities.default: 1k creates/s, 50k redirects/s at peak (design target); 100M links/year

ambiguities.question: What does 'fast' mean for redirects?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Sets the latency budget for the hot path and whether a cache is mandatory.
options: p99 redirect latency < 50 ms (server side) with cache
ambiguities.default: p99 redirect latency < 50 ms (server side) with cache

ambiguities.question: Which analytics are required?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Determines the event model, storage growth and whether raw click events are kept.
options: detailed: total clicks, clicks per day, top referrers
basic: total clicks and last click time
ambiguities.default: detailed: total clicks, clicks per day, top referrers

ambiguities.question: Are user accounts (sign-up, login, per-user link ownership) in scope for this iteration?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Adds identity, authorization on every endpoint and a users table; roughly doubles scope.
options: out of scope for v1 (anonymous API); design leaves room for ownership
in scope: accounts and per-user links
ambiguities.default: out of scope for v1 (anonymous API); design leaves room for ownership

ambiguities.question: Should clients be able to choose a custom alias?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Adds alias validation, reserved words and a conflict (409) path.

ambiguities.question: Should links support an optional expiry?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Adds a nullable expires_at column and a 410 Gone response.

ambiguities.question: Should link creation be rate limited to prevent abuse?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Public shorteners are abused for spam/phishing; protects storage and reputation.

acceptance_criteria: POST /api/v1/links returns 201 with code and short_url for a valid URL, 400 for an invalid one
GET /{code} returns 302 with Location for a known code and 404 for an unknown one
Creating many links concurrently yields unique codes and never overwrites an existing link
Click counts reported by the stats endpoint equal the number of redirects served
Every route in the implementation is documented in the OpenAPI contract and vice versa
